text:
[IRET.8.2] **Refraction.** A terminal node maintains a
refraction table: the set of token *identities* for which
an activation has already fired and not been re-created, keyed by
token hash (pre-filter) plus the fact-id tuple (the key);
see `[IRET.11.3]` for the full contract and the
identity-tiebreak rationale. On activation fire, the
token identity is added to the refraction table. On
re-activation (same token, after the fact that caused it
changed), refraction state for that identity is cleared ([IRET.11.3.2]).

idris.name: iret_11_3__refraction_after_history
idris.note: The clause's rule -- an identity's refraction state is cleared on re-activation, and the table holds the identities that fired and were not re-created -- is the flag in the tick-free fragment: re-activation creates an unfired activation, and a fired one keeps its flag until then ([IRET.11.3.2]).

idris.name: iret_8_2__activated_unfired
idris.note: ON RE-ACTIVATION THE IDENTITY IS NOT REFRACTED: every activation a terminal gains is unfired, which is the clause's 'refraction state for that identity is cleared'.

idris.name: iret_8_2__insert_act_inv
idris.note: An activation of the list after an insert is the inserted one or an old one.

idris.name: rdsc_4a_5__load_g
idris.note: The table before any firing: the loaded network with an empty set, no identity having fired.

idris.name: rdsc_4a_5__load_sound
idris.note: The loaded network with the empty set is sound.
